lean.statement: For measurable spaces A, B and C, a probability measure μ on A, Markov kernels K and L from A to B, a Markov kernel S from B to C, and a real function ε integrable under μ: if for μ-almost every x, every measurable set s satisfies |(K x).real s - (L x).real s| ≤ ε x, then every measurable set t satisfies |((S ∘ₖ K) ∘ₘ μ).real t - ((S ∘ₖ L) ∘ₘ μ).real t| ≤ ∫ x, ε x ∂μ.
approved_definition_context: Kernel composition first applies the right-hand kernel and then the left-hand kernel; composing a kernel with an input measure integrates the resulting conditional law.
Every displayed kernel is a Markov probability kernel, so all conditional event masses lie between zero and one.
The same downstream kernel occurs on both sides; no claim is made for two different downstream transitions.
An integrable real budget can depend on the input and bounds every measurable-event discrepancy almost everywhere.
